A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SODP and contain complete, readable main texts and appendices. Their methods, experiments, equations, figures, and tables can be reliably matched despite additions and relocations in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original SODP experiments on Meta-World and Adroit, including success rates, learning curves, ablations, and per-task returns in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds offline-to-online comparisons, an Adroit regularization ablation, computational timings, and pre-training performance comparisons.

M1.justification: The diffusion pre-training objective, reward-based fine-tuning, BC regularizer, architecture, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Expanded explanations and adaptations of comparison methods do not revise SODP.

E1.justification: Both versions cover MT50-rand, MT10, image-based Meta-World and Adroit, differing pre-training data quality, and transfer to unseen tasks. The added experiments reuse existing task and observation coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix C.3/Table 7 substantially expands the offline-to-online comparisons with MT-DQL, MT-IDQL, and deterministic and stochastic MT-ODT. v2 already evaluates offline MTDQL and MTDT, but not these online-fine-tuned comparisons. Existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Added experiments specify offline BC followed by online actor/critic tuning for diffusion baselines, 1M online steps per task for DT variants, and matched Adroit fine-tuning with and without BC. The timing protocol measures 1M environment steps and 50 evaluation episodes on shared hardware. Retained experiments' settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantive analyses of BC's contribution on image-based Adroit (Table 9), computational cost (Table 11), and the contributions of pre-training versus fine-tuning across four methods (Table 12). The scratch-training ablation and Figure 7 move from v2 Appendix C.2 to Section 5.5 and are not new evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain mean and standard-deviation reporting across three seeds, five-seed learning curves, and episode-level return variability. Added results use the existing reporting practices; no changed run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Matched existing results are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial new result entries. Table 7 reports MT-ODT_stoc at 50.47±0.21 against SODP's retained MT10 score of 65.27±0.21. Table 9 adds Adroit pre-training and no-BC averages of 34.3 and 43.7 alongside the retained 73.9 with BC. Tables 11–12 add timings and pre-training success rates. These are additional comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.1 introduces a linear-MDP setup, feature covariance matrix, and UCB exploration-bonus definition to connect SODP with cited reward-free exploration guarantees. This adds formal background, but no SODP-specific theorem or proof; the existing derivations in Appendix A remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: learning a versatile diffusion planner from sub-optimal data, task-specific reward fine-tuning, BC regularization, and effective downstream adaptation. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1 newly interprets SODP through reward-free exploration and suggests preservation of sample-efficiency and robustness properties. Appendix C.3 attributes stochastic DT's advantage to exploration and its remaining gap to diffusion's action diversity. These extend the explanatory arguments; existing applicability qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 for the timing comparison and reports per-task resource costs, including SODP's 11–13 hours for fine-tuning and 47 seconds for 50 evaluation episodes. It also describes the added baseline adaptations. Existing SODP hyperparameters and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning through reward-free and count-based exploration, citing Wang and Jin (2020) and Ostrovski (2017), plus related diffusion work by He and Yuan (2024). Bai (2025) replaces Glaese (2022) in the alignment motivation. Numerous other reference changes update publication metadata for the same works.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized prose expansions and reorganizes Section 5.5 around the relocated pre-training ablation. It adds appendix subsections, acknowledgements, an impact statement, and affiliation/publication updates. Most of the original narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds four compact tables (7, 9, 11, and 12), relocates Figure 7 into the main text, and reflows or renumbers existing tables. Existing figure content and the overall visual design are preserved, without a substantial graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: The added online-fine-tuned generative baselines address a comparison gap in v2, while the Adroit BC ablation and pre-training comparisons strengthen empirical support. Timing results improve transparency about SODP's greater computational cost. These provide a limited net improvement, although Appendix B.1's suggestion that theoretical properties transfer to SODP is not established by a corresponding proof.
